name: Future Islands
label: 4AD
lede: Three friends from eastern North Carolina played show after show for eight years before four minutes on Letterman, a chest-thump and a growl, made the whole country ask who Sam Herring was.

eras.title: Before the name, a white suit
eras.text: Before Future Islands there was Art Lord & the Self-Portraits, a performance-art band from East Carolina University in Greenville. Sam Herring and Gerrit Welmers had been friends since eighth grade in Morehead City, and art-school classmate William Cashion had helped Herring cram for an art history exam.

years.h: Art Lord & the Self-Portraits open at Soccer Moms' House
years.p: Valentine's Day, a Greenville house, and Sam Herring in a 1970s white suit as Locke Ernst-Frost, a narcissistic artist. The show is remembered as tumultuous.
years.xp:
The character's name mashed up the philosopher John Locke, the painter Max Ernst and the poet Robert Frost. The line-up: Herring on vocals, Gerrit Welmers on keyboards, William Cashion on guitar then bass, Adam Beeby on rhythmic keyboards and Kymia Nawabi on percussion and backing vocals.

Herring later said he fell in love with performance art at 17. Art Lord was where that came out.

years.h: Kymia Nawabi leaves Art Lord to finish her degree
years.p: Nawabi, a senior, quits in mid-2003 to work on her graduation project. She later painted the covers for five Future Islands records.

years.h: Adam Beeby moves away and Art Lord ends with him
years.p: Beeby, the band's rhythmic keyboardist, leaves Greenville in September 2005. Art Lord & the Self-Portraits falls apart within months.

eras.title: Two names, one tour date
eras.text: The three of them regrouped as Future Islands to keep a tour date, added a drummer on electronic drums, and made records cheaply and fast. Then Herring hit a wall and left town for a year.

q: we combined them to Future Islands.
years.h: Future Islands play their first show at an anti-Valentine's party
years.p: William Cashion on the name: the choices were Already Islands or Future Shoes. The show, at a Greenville house called Turducken, filled a tour slot with alt-country band The Texas Governor.
years.xp:
The line-up was Sam Herring, Gerrit Welmers, Cashion and Erick Murillo on electronic drums.

The band had been formed weeks earlier to honor that tour commitment, and kept going after it.

years.h: First EP Little Advances goes out self-released
years.p: Recorded in March 2006, three months after the band's first show.

years.h: Herring walks out of East Carolina University and into Asheville
years.p: He leaves school in June 2006. He later said he got sucked into the partying, and it took about a year to get his act together.

years.h: Backdoor Skateshop turns studio for three days
years.p: The band records its first album in Greenville with Chester Endersby Gwazda in July 2007. Cashion later said they spent about a month mixing it.
years.xp: Cashion's account: "we recorded the whole album in 3 days, spent about a month mixing it." The album was Wave Like Home; it came out a year later.

years.h: Drummer Erick Murillo quits after a Halloween party
years.p: Murillo leaves in autumn 2007. Future Islands carries on as a trio, with a drum machine.

eras.title: Baltimore takes them in
eras.text: Dan Deacon pointed them to Baltimore: cheap rent, and easy drives to New York, Philadelphia and D.C. They toured hard, Herring's long relationship ended, and the breakup became the first of two albums on Thrill Jockey.

years.cap: Sam Herring at a Baltimore show, January 2008
years.h: Dan Deacon's advice sends them to Baltimore
years.p: Deacon and Benny Boeldt of Adventure push. William Cashion moves in November 2007, Sam Herring in January 2008, Gerrit Welmers later that year.

years.h: Wave Like Home arrives a year late on Upset The Rhythm
years.p: London's Upset The Rhythm puts out the debut album, with a Kymia Nawabi cover.

years.h: Back-to-back tours end Herring's long relationship
years.p: After consecutive national tours, Sam Herring's relationship of years is over. The songs he writes straight afterward become In Evening Air.

years.cap: Sam Herring at Point Ephemere, Paris, October 5, 2010
years.h: A drunk spectator tackles Herring in Paris and tears his ACL
years.p: The tour is behind Dan Deacon's Bromst, and Herring doesn't find out about the ligament until six months later.
years.xp:
Herring was on the road with the Dan Deacon Ensemble when a spectator in Paris tackled him. The knee turned out to have a torn ACL.

He had surgery in February 2010 and played Amoeba that June in a brace.

years.h: A four-song demo travels from Double Dagger to Thrill Jockey
years.p: Bruce Willen of Baltimore's [[Double Dagger|6b35f310-3ba2-4fef-afa2-33f5cc706652]] passes along Tin Man, Walking Through That Door, Long Flight and As I Fall. The label signs the band.

years.h: In Evening Air comes out of a Baltimore living room
years.p: Recorded in July 2009 in Marble Hill with Chester Endersby Gwazda, and out on Thrill Jockey nine months later.
years.xp: The same year brought the In the Fall EP with Katrina Ford of Celebration, The Post Office Chapel Wave EP with [[No Age|55821c25-bd47-4f67-baf8-17ccd2cf1c86]] and [[Beach House|d5cc67b8-1cc4-453b-96e8-44487acdebea]]'s Victoria Legrand, and Undressed, recorded July 7, 2010 at Mobtown Studios.

years.h: Ten days in a friend's house make On the Water
years.p: [[Jenn Wasner|c7616574-4d5d-425d-b45e-5b9392e8661c]] of [[Wye Oak|3c8ff4c9-b5b9-4e78-ad9d-5157c323de24]] duets on The Great Fire. The house is in Elizabeth City, North Carolina.
years.xp: It wasn't all calm. Sam Herring recalled someone from the label hanging around during writing, talking about deadlines: "Can we not talk about business while writing a song?"

years.cap: Future Islands at the Beachland Tavern, Cleveland, February 2011
years.h: After a year touring On the Water, they walk away from Thrill Jockey
years.p: Singles follow on Upset The Rhythm and Famous Class.
years.xp: Thrill Jockey had released two Future Islands albums, In Evening Air and On the Water. The band never went back.

eras.title: Four minutes on Letterman
eras.text: Five straight years on the road, then a hunting cabin, a deal with 4AD and a record called Singles. One TV spot turned a hard-working band into a worldwide story, and Herring's body paid for the tour that followed.

years.h: The band disappears into a rented hunting cabin to write
years.p: February to July 2013, in rural North Carolina. About eight songs got written there; three made the record.
years.xp: Herring said they demoed "about 24 or 25 songs" and settled on a ten-track record. The cabin stretch overlapped with rehearsals for Art Lord & the Self-Portraits' tenth anniversary show.

years.h: Chris Coady produces the next record at Dreamland in Hurley, New York
years.p: The band records in August 2013 under a new three-album deal with 4AD.

years.h: Herring pounds his chest on Letterman and the clip goes everywhere
years.p: Future Islands plays Seasons (Waiting on You) on March 3. It becomes the most-viewed video on the show's YouTube channel.
years.xp:
Herring danced, pounded his chest and dropped into a guttural growl, and the clip spread everywhere within days. David Letterman came over afterward delighted.

Critics later called it one of the great live TV performances.

years.h: Singles lands three weeks later on 4AD
years.p: The collage cover is by Beth Hoeckel.

q: Basically, I was four for four.
years.h: Herring's doctor finds Reinke's edema
years.p: The vocal cords swell. Herring listed the four causes: acid reflux, smoking, talking too much and misusing the voice.
years.xp: To get through shows he leaned harder on the growl, which became one of his trademarks.

years.cap: Sam Herring at Positivus Festival, Latvia, July 2014
years.h: Herring passes out at an airport and still plays Primavera Sound
years.p: Exhausted, he goes down on the way to the festival. Medics revive him and he makes the flight.

years.h: Pitchfork, NME and Pazz & Jop all pick Seasons for 2014
years.p: Consequence of Sound and the Village Voice's critics' poll join them.

years.h: Jim Eno records The Chase and Haunted by You in Austin
years.p: The two-song single is cut at Public Hi-Fi with [[Spoon|84eac621-1c5a-49a1-9500-555099c6e184]]'s [[Jim Eno|402a60a2-65cb-4f79-870f-7f9ffdf3bb20]].

years.cap: Sam Herring at Kosmonaut Festival, Chemnitz, June 2015
years.h: Herring does a knee drop at Red Rocks and tears a meniscus
years.p: The show is the opening slot for [[Morrissey|013fa897-86db-41d3-8e9f-386c8a34f4e6]]. He plays the last four months of the Singles tour on it.

eras.title: The long road after the viral clip
eras.text: A drummer on record, big-name producers, festival stages and TV again. Herring kept writing about love coming apart, most nakedly about a long-distance relationship lost to lockdown.

years.h: Secret shows under fake names test the new songs
years.p: After writing in a four-story beach house in Avon, on the Outer Banks, they play as The Hidden Haven, This Old House and Chirping Bush.
years.xp: The Hidden Haven was the beach house. This Old House was a TV show Herring watched growing up. Chirping Bush came from Gerrit Welmers' dream about birds stuck in a bush.

years.h: The Far Field brings Debbie Harry and a full-time drummer
years.p: Recorded at Sunset Sound in Los Angeles with John Congleton. Michael Lowry of [[Lake Trout|08b14860-14fb-454e-a83d-8178174d7d90]] joins on drums, Debbie Harry of [[Blondie|4d2956d1-a3f7-44bb-9a41-67563e1a0c94]] sings, Kymia Nawabi paints the cover.
years.xp: The title and themes come from the poet Theodore Roethke. Michael Lowry, from the Baltimore bands Lake Trout and Mt. Royal, became a core member after years of Future Islands using touring drummers.

years.h: As Long as You Are arrives in the middle of a pandemic
years.p: The third 4AD album. For Sure later lands in the MLB The Show 21 soundtrack.
years.xp: Michael Lowry was now a core member. Singles came first: For Sure on July 8, Thrill on August 12 and Moonlight on September 15.

years.h: Colbert has them play King of Sweden
years.p: Eight years after Letterman, Future Islands is back at the Ed Sullivan Theater.

years.h: Weezer takes them out on Indie Rock Road Trip
years.p: Future Islands supports [[Weezer|6fe07aa5-fec0-4eca-a456-f29bff451b04]] on several dates of the 2023 tour.

years.h: People Who Aren't There Anymore follows one breakup across lockdowns
years.p: The seventh album was written and recorded during COVID-19, about the end of Sam Herring's long-distance relationship.

years.h: A rarities collection and a May tour go on the calendar
years.p: From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth collects deep cuts, rarities and live tracks, scheduled for May 22, 2026, with a North American tour that month.
